top_signals.title: Citi’s $60 Oil Call Meets $112 Brent
top_signals.summary: Citi sees more upside risk for oil prices despite recovering Middle Eastern crude exports, a considerably less bearish assessment from the bank that predicted $60-to-$65 Brent by year-end just three months ago. Brent December futures traded at $111.70 on Thursday, up $2.88, or 2.65%, after touching $112.68 earlier in the session. The problem, Citi says, is that getting crude out of the Gulf and getting it to buyers at a reasonable cost are two different things. top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.
